offices.title: Little Office of the Holy Name of God

sourceHeadings.title: From The Manual of the Archconfraternity of the Holy Face (1887)

introductoryNotes.text: From The Manual of the Archconfraternity of the Holy Face (1887)

The Little Office of the Most Holy Name of God is largely attributed to the pen of Mr Dupont. It was originally discovered in a pamphlet entitled Association of Prayers Against Blasphemy, which went through several editions, the last known being published in 1867. Since then, it appears not to have been reissued. Given its devotional and historical significance, it seems fitting to preserve this portion. We therefore present it here as a supplement to our manual of the archconfraternity, from which it may easily be detached and issued as a separate tract.

This Office serves as an act of reparation and homage to the Most Holy and Adorable Name of God—a Name so often misunderstood and profaned in our times. It is known that many devout souls in the world have already adopted the practice of reciting this Little Office daily. Such a praiseworthy example deserves the highest commendation, and it is our earnest hope that many others will follow, so that a sacred chorus of praise may rise to counter the dreadful clamour which, in our day, is so grievously directed against God and His most awe-inspiring Name.

introductoryNotes.text: 1 Diversis anni temporibus Officium parvum variis modis dicendum est. Aliter per Annum, aliter in Adventu, aliter post Nativitatem, atque Tempore Paschali aliter, sicut in cujusque loco videri potest. Quae sequentia sunt notanda:
introductoryNotes.english: 1. At different times of the year the Little Office is to be said in different forms: one form during the year, another in Advent, another after the Nativity, and another in Eastertide, as can be seen in each appropriate place. The following points should be noted:

introductoryNotes.text: I Per Annum dicitur
introductoryNotes.english: I. The form During the Year is said:

introductoryNotes.text: a) A Matutinis 3 Februarii usque ad Nonam Sabbati sancti inclusive (Festo Annuntiationis excepto), ac b) A Vesperis in Sabbato Quatuor Temporum Pentecostes usque ad Nonam Sabbati ante Dominicam I Adventus pariter inclusive.
introductoryNotes.english: a) From Matins on 3 February through None on Holy Saturday, inclusive, except on the Feast of the Annunciation; and b) from Vespers on the Ember Saturday of Pentecost through None on the Saturday before the First Sunday of Advent, likewise inclusive.

introductoryNotes.text: II In Adventu dicitur
introductoryNotes.english: II. The form In Advent is said:

introductoryNotes.text: a) A Vesperis ante Dominicam I Adventus usque ad Nonam Vigiliae Nativitatis inclusive, ac in b) Festo Annuntiationis.
introductoryNotes.english: a) From Vespers before the First Sunday of Advent through None on the Vigil of the Nativity, inclusive; and b) on the Feast of the Annunciation.

introductoryNotes.text: III Post Nativitatem dicitur
introductoryNotes.english: III. The form After the Nativity is said:

introductoryNotes.text: A Vesperis diei 24 Decembris usque ad Completorium diei 2 Februarii inclusive.
introductoryNotes.english: From Vespers on 24 December through Compline on 2 February, inclusive.

introductoryNotes.text: IV Tempore Paschali dicitur
introductoryNotes.english: IV. The form In Eastertide is said:

introductoryNotes.text: A Vesperis Sabbati sancti usque ad Nonam Sabbati Quatuor Temporum Pentecostes inclusive.
introductoryNotes.english: From Vespers on Holy Saturday through None on the Ember Saturday of Pentecost, inclusive.

introductoryNotes.text: 2 Differentiae Tempore Paschali occurrentes ob majorem commoditatem intra corpus Officii I Per Annum mixtae sunt; quae autem In Adventu et Post Nativitatem veniunt, post Officium inveniuntur. 3 (Alleluja) et (Alleluja, alleluja) in Officio Per Annum, solum Tempore Paschali dicuntur. 4 Si Festum Annuntiationis Tempore Paschali venerit, dicitur, sicut notatum est, Officium ut In Adventu; sed cum Alleluja et stropha Quaesumus, Auctor omnium. 5 Gloria Patri Triduo ante Pascha etiam dicitur.
introductoryNotes.english: 2. For greater convenience, the differences occurring in Eastertide are incorporated into the body of Office I, During the Year; those occurring in Advent and After the Nativity are found after that office. 3. The parenthetical “Alleluia” and “Alleluia, alleluia” in the office During the Year are said only in Eastertide. 4. introductoryNotes.text: From The Manual of the Augustinian Secular Tertiaries (1927)

The “Serotina Prayers” for our Community and Benefactors. It is the custom of the Servants of God to prayer specifically for living and deceased benefactors. The prayers which follow, called the “Serotina” (evening time prayers) are prayers traditionally said by Augustinian communities for their living and deceased benefactors. At some point in the day, the brother/sister takes time to pray for the good of his/her family and for his/her living and deceased benefactors. This “office” is particularly useful to begin or end common meetings.
